header: A PICTURE OPENED OVER THE PAGE, NOT IN A NEW TAB: the same kind of layer as the circular viewer (src/components/CircularViewerLightbox.tsx): a dark full-screen layer above everything (above the search window too), the picture as large as the screen allows with its caption and credit, a cross (and Escape, and a click outside the picture) to close it and be back exactly where you were. I keep it free of any topic name: any card may open a picture in it.
* I draw it in a portal on <body>, so that the search window's own scaling and clipping cannot shrink or cut it, and it sits above the window (z 400).

* Escape closes the PICTURE ONLY. The search window behind it closes on Escape in two places: TopBar's own capture handler on window (which lets an Escape pass when it comes from inside an element marked data-escape-own, as the calculators' dropdown is marked data-select-open), and OmnibarModal's handler. The layer carries data-escape-own (so TopBar leaves that Escape alone) and I take the key in the capture phase and stop it (so OmnibarModal never sees it). The next Escape closes the window, as before.
* I lock the page's scrolling while it is open (the shared lock, src/lib/ui/scrollLock.ts) and move the focus to the cross, then back to the thumbnail that opened it.
* I give the picture NO background colour of its own: a white one showed as a pale fringe where the picture's edge fell on a half pixel. What shows round it is the dark layer.

* I show the size of the picture as it is (for example 606 x 438 px) so that nobody mistakes a small original for a poor display. A picture that is smaller than the screen is shown ENLARGED to fill the layer, up to twice its own size (fitSize), and the caption then says so ("shown 1.8 times larger"); a picture larger than the layer is shrunk to fit. It is never cropped.

behaviours: the layer is a modal dialog named by the picture's title, above everything (z 400, over the search window's own layers), dark, full screen
it has a cross that closes it, with a name a screen reader can read
it shows the picture itself, as large as the screen allows and never cropped (object-contain, max height and width of the layer), with its title, its date tag and its credit
it says the size of the picture as it is, so that a small original is not mistaken for a poor display (1209 × 795 px)
the enlarged picture has no background colour of its own (a white one showed as a pale fringe where the picture's edge fell on a half pixel); the dark layer shows round it
a link to open the file in a new tab is NOT there: the picture stays in the layer (no anchor, no target=_blank)
a click on the dark area closes it: the area is a button behind the picture (out of the tab order, named Close the picture), and the picture and its credit sit above it and do not close it
a small picture (606 × 438) is enlarged to fill the room, the height being the limit here: 1.83 times, 1107 × 800, never cropped
a very small picture is enlarged at most twice (200 × 200 -> 400 × 400), so that it is not stretched into a blur
a picture about as large as the room is shown at about its own size (1209 × 795 -> 1217 × 800)
a picture larger than the room is shrunk to fit, with the same proportions (1209 × 795 into 600 × 500 -> 600 × 395)
no room or no size yet gives nothing (the picture then shows at its own size, limited to the layer)
the caption says the real size and that the picture is shown enlarged ('606 × 438 px, shown 1.8 times larger'); the picture takes the computed size
a picture shown at about its own size does not claim to be enlarged
another key does nothing to the picture and reaches the page as usual
Escape closes the picture and is NOT seen by the search window's handler (it stays open; the next Escape closes it)
once the picture is closed, Escape goes back to the page (the handler is let go)
the layer is marked data-escape-own, and TopBar leaves an Escape that comes from inside such an element alone (as it does for an open dropdown)
the story card opens its pictures and portraits in this layer: no link to a picture file with target=_blank is left
